newsitem.title: USA: Mich. Gov. declares emergency following storms.
newsitem.headline: Mich. Gov. declares emergency following storms.

text.p: Michigan Gov. John Engler on Thursday declared a state of emergency for Detroit and the nearby area after powerful thunderstorms slammed southeast Michigan and left at least eight people dead.

Engler, who planned to survey damage with Detroit Mayor Dennis Archer later in the day, said he would ask for an advance team from the Federal Emergency Management Agency to start the process of applying for federal disaster aid.

"The damage is extensive and it's going to be costly," he told a news conference. "Right now on the ground the key thing is to restore access to roads, get the wires up and out of the way and the safety hazards reduced."
Destruction across the southeastern corner of the state was massive and widespread after a storm with winds up to 100 mph (160 km) whipped through the area on Wednesday afternoon.

In the exclusive community of Gross Pointe Farms, five people on a summer picnic who were huddling in a gazebo for shelter were killed when high winds ripped the structure out of the ground and tossed it into nearby Lake St. Clair.
Two others were killed in Oakland County, one when a mobile home collapsed after being struck by a tornado. Another person was killed in Flint, Michigan, by a falling tree.

In Plymouth, west of Detroit in Oakland County, a local courthouse was destroyed by a raging fire caused by downed power lines. In Hamtramck, a working class community bordering Detroit, roofs were torn off entire blocks of homes. Trees were uprooted and shattered glass littered streets.
"We got hit pretty hard. In all my years in Hamtramck I've never seen anything like this," said Mayor Robert Kozaren. "It's a complete disaster."
Detroit Police spokesman Bill Ratliff said the death toll could rise, with some possible fatalities in the city.
Detroit Edison Co. said about 200,000 people were without power on Thursday morning. Outages knocked out roadway pumps, which led to flooding and traffic snarls throughout the area.
A stepped-up police presence led to a mostly quiet night, but Archer said he would ask judges to deal severely with those who have been caught looting.
Although there were numerous tornado sightings, the only confirmed tornado to touch down was near a mobile home park outside of Holly, about 50 miles (80 km) northwest of Detroit.
